-- @inline Main.consume never
-- @inline Main.consumeDown never
-- @inline Main.consumeZero never
-- @inline Main.consumeMultiple never
-- @inline Main.withUnknown never
-- @inline Main.withExtraUse never
-- @inline Main.withInterveningEffect never
-- @inline Main.increase never
-- @inline Main.decrease never
-- @inline Main.normalize never
-- @inline Main.multiple never
-- @inline Main.observe never
module Main where

import Prelude
import Data.Foldable (for_)
import Effect (Effect)
import Effect.Console (logShow)
import Effect.Ref as Ref

type Snapshot = { alpha :: Int, beta :: Int, delta :: Int, gamma :: Int, iota :: Int, omega :: Int, theta :: Int, zeta :: Int }

make :: Int -> Snapshot
make seed = { alpha: seed, beta: seed + 1, delta: seed + 2, gamma: seed + 3, iota: seed + 4, omega: seed + 5, theta: seed + 6, zeta: seed + 7 }

total :: Snapshot -> Int
total row = row.alpha + row.beta + row.delta + row.gamma + row.iota + row.omega + row.theta + row.zeta

increase :: Int -> Snapshot -> Snapshot
increase 0 row = row
increase remaining row = increase (remaining - 1) (row { theta = row.theta + 1 })

decrease :: Int -> Snapshot -> Snapshot
decrease 0 row = row
decrease remaining row = decrease (remaining - 1) (row { beta = row.beta - 1 })

normalize :: Int -> Snapshot -> Snapshot
normalize 0 row = row
normalize remaining row = normalize (remaining - 1) (row { gamma = row.gamma + 0 })

multiple :: Int -> Snapshot -> Snapshot
multiple 0 row = row
multiple remaining row = multiple (remaining - 1) (row { delta = row.delta + 3, zeta = row.zeta - 2 })

consume :: Int -> Ref.Ref Snapshot -> Effect Int
consume count reference = do
  original <- Ref.read reference
  let changed = increase count original
  pure (total changed + total original)

consumeDown :: Int -> Ref.Ref Snapshot -> Effect Int
consumeDown count reference = do
  original <- Ref.read reference
  let changed = decrease count original
  pure (total changed + total original)

consumeZero :: Int -> Ref.Ref Snapshot -> Effect Int
consumeZero count reference = do
  original <- Ref.read reference
  let changed = normalize count original
  pure (total changed + total original)

consumeMultiple :: Int -> Ref.Ref Snapshot -> Effect Int
consumeMultiple count reference = do
  original <- Ref.read reference
  let changed = multiple count original
  pure (total changed + total original)

observe :: Snapshot -> Int
observe row = row.theta + 11

withUnknown :: Int -> Ref.Ref Snapshot -> Effect Int
withUnknown count reference = do
  original <- Ref.read reference
  let changed = increase count original
  pure (total changed + observe changed + total original)

withExtraUse :: Int -> Ref.Ref Snapshot -> Effect (Array Int)
withExtraUse count reference = do
  original <- Ref.read reference
  let changed = increase count original
  pure [ total changed + total original, changed.theta ]

withInterveningEffect :: Int -> Ref.Ref Snapshot -> Effect Int
withInterveningEffect count reference = do
  original <- Ref.read reference
  let changed = increase count original
  Ref.write (make 700) reference
  fresh <- Ref.read reference
  pure (total changed + total original + total fresh)

main :: Effect Unit
main = do
  seeds <- Ref.new [ 0, -2147483648, 2147483647, -9 ]
  counts <- Ref.new [ 0, 1, 2, 7, 31 ]
  inputs <- Ref.read seeds
  amounts <- Ref.read counts
  for_ inputs \seed -> for_ amounts \count -> do
    reference <- Ref.new (make seed)
    up <- consume count reference
    down <- consumeDown count reference
    zero <- consumeZero count reference
    both <- consumeMultiple count reference
    unknown <- withUnknown count reference
    extra <- withExtraUse count reference
    original <- Ref.read reference
    logShow [ up, down, zero, both, unknown, total original ]
    logShow extra
  reference <- Ref.new (make 5)
  let saved = consume 7 reference
  saved >>= logShow
  Ref.write (make 19) reference
  saved >>= logShow
  withInterveningEffect 2 reference >>= logShow
  Ref.read reference >>= (logShow <<< total)

"""Separate AB/BA/AB diagnostics for primary increases, preserving primary samples."""
from pathlib import Path
import argparse, difflib, hashlib, json, math, os, re, runpy, statistics, subprocess, sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone

ROOT = Path('/Users/0x1/Documents/htdocs/altbak.pub')

PROOF = WORK / 'proofs/isolated-regressions'
HELPERS = runpy.run_path(str(Path(__file__).with_name('compare-generated.py')))
def function_body(source,name):
    text=source.decode() if isinstance(source,bytes) else source
    start=text.index('func '+name+'(')
    opening=text.index('{',start)
    depth=0
    pattern=r'"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"|`[^`]*`|\'(?:\\.|[^\'\\])*\'|//[^\n]*|/\*[\s\S]*?\*/|[{}]'
    for token in re.finditer(pattern,text[opening:]):
        if token[0]=='{':depth+=1
        elif token[0]=='}':
            depth-=1
            if depth==0:return text[opening:opening+token.end()]
    raise ValueError('Unterminated generated function '+name)


sha = lambda path: hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
primary = WORK / 'campaign/results.json'
primary_sha = sha(primary)
report = json.loads(primary.read_text())
labels = [row['case'] for row in report['rows_by_go_c_descending'] if row['change_percent'] > 5]
assert labels, 'No primary increases need diagnostics'
rows = {row['case']: row for row in report['rows_by_go_c_descending']}
assert all(rows[label]['change_percent'] > 5 for label in labels)
cases = []
for label in labels:
    row = report['all_campaign']['all_tests'][label]
    core = label in report['primary_times_us']['after']
    cases.append({'key': re.sub(r'[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]+', '-', label), 'label': label,
                  'module': row['module'].replace('.', '_'),
                  'getter': 'Get_' + row['module'].replace('.', '_') + ('_act' if core else '_prepare'),
                  'expected': row['expected'], 'prepare': not core, 'source_suite': 'core' if core else 'all',
                  'primary_change_percent': rows[label]['change_percent']})
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
parser.add_argument('--execute', action='store_true')
args = parser.parse_args()
if not args.execute:
    print(json.dumps({'cases': cases, 'primary_sha256': primary_sha, 'processes': 6 * len(cases), 'executed': False}, indent=2))
    raise SystemExit(0)
builds = {scope: {side: WORK / (side + '-' + scope) for side in ('before', 'after')} for scope in ('core', 'all')}
env = dict(os.environ, GOGC='800', GOWORK='off')
for key in ['GOMAXPROCS', 'PPROF', 'GOFLAGS', 'GOEXPERIMENT']:
    env.pop(key, None)
PROOF.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
(PROOF / 'inputs.json').write_text(json.dumps(cases, indent=2) + '\n')
inventories = {scope: {side: HELPERS['inventory'](path) for side, path in pair.items()} for scope, pair in builds.items()}
originals = {scope: {side: inventory['provenance'] for side, inventory in pair.items()} for scope, pair in inventories.items()}
commands, sources, comparisons = {}, {}, {}


def normalize(body):
    # Canonicalize only generated package aliases/runtime spelling and trailing
    # whitespace; preserve calls, literals, arithmetic, local names and order.
    body = re.sub(r'\b(?:g[0-9a-f]{6})\.', 'package.', body.decode())
    body = re.sub(r'\br_\.', 'r.', body)
    return '\n'.join(line.rstrip() for line in body.splitlines()).strip() + '\n'


# First compare target module and original harness sections, before building probes.
for case in cases:
    key = case['key']
    selected = {'Bench.go', 'Bench_ffi.go', 'Effect_Console.go', 'Effect_Console_ffi.go', case['module'] + '.go'}
    extracted = {side: {name: body for name, body in inventory['sections'].items() if Path(name).name in selected}
                 for side, inventory in inventories[case['source_suite']].items()}
    assert set(extracted['before']) == set(extracted['after'])
    comparisons[key] = {'source_suite': case['source_suite'], 'sections': {}}
    for name in extracted['before']:
        old, new = extracted['before'][name], extracted['after'][name]
        a, b = normalize(old), normalize(new)
        comparisons[key]['sections'][name] = {'before_sha256': hashlib.sha256(old).hexdigest(),
                                              'after_sha256': hashlib.sha256(new).hexdigest(),
                                              'byte_identical': old == new, 'normalized_identical': a == b,
                                              'before': old.decode(), 'after': new.decode(),
                                              'normalized_diff': ''.join(difflib.unified_diff(a.splitlines(True), b.splitlines(True)))}
    for name,item in comparisons[key]['sections'].items():
        if item['byte_identical']:
            continue
        assert Path(name).name=='Bench.go', ('Changed target/harness code',key,name)
        old,new=item['before'],item['after']
        old_body=function_body(old,'Call_Bench_runBench')
        new_body=function_body(new,'Call_Bench_runBench')
        assert old.replace(old_body,'<runBench-body>')==new.replace(new_body,'<runBench-body>')
        proof=json.loads((WORK/'proofs/generated-workload-review.json').read_text())[case['source_suite']]
        assert proof['runBench_only_ten_measureBatch_call_lowerings_and_local_renaming']
        assert hashlib.sha256(old_body.encode()).hexdigest()==proof['old_runBench_sha256']
        assert hashlib.sha256(new_body.encode()).hexdigest()==proof['new_runBench_sha256']
        assert proof['timed_loop_and_callback_adapter_unchanged']
        item['measureBatch_call_lowering_outside_timer_verified']=True
        item['lowering_note']='Generic direct worker for the same ten calls, same arguments and order; conversions occur before the unchanged timed thunk.'
    run_before=next(body for body in inventories[case['source_suite']]['before']['sections'].values() if b'func Call_Bench_runBench(' in body)
    run_after=next(body for body in inventories[case['source_suite']]['after']['sections'].values() if b'func Call_Bench_runBench(' in body)
    unchanged_runbench = function_body(run_before,'Call_Bench_runBench') == function_body(run_after,'Call_Bench_runBench')
    comparisons[key]['runBench_byte_identical']=unchanged_runbench
    comparisons[key]['runBench_only_outside_timer_call_lowering']=not unchanged_runbench
    comparisons[key]['timed_measureBatch_identical']=True
    assert all(item['byte_identical'] for name,item in comparisons[key]['sections'].items() if Path(name).name=='Bench_ffi.go')
    comparisons[key]['measureBatch_ffi_identical']=True
(PROOF / 'generated-comparison.json').write_text(json.dumps(comparisons, indent=2) + '\n')
print('Target and timed harness verified; see exact generated-comparison.json.', flush=True)

for case in cases:
    key = case['key']
    commands[key], sources[key] = {}, {}
    for side, inventory in inventories[case['source_suite']].items():
        owner = lambda name: [str(Path(path).parent) for path, body in inventory['sections'].items()
                              if re.search(rb'func ' + name.encode() + rb'\(', body)]
        action, bench, console = owner(case['getter']), owner('Call_Bench_runBench'), owner('Get_Effect_Console_log')
        assert len(action) == len(bench) == len(console) == 1
        packages = sorted(set(action + bench + console))
        aliases = {name: 'p' + str(i) for i, name in enumerate(packages)}
        imports = '; '.join(aliases[name] + ' "gopurs/output/' + name + '"' for name in packages)
        act = aliases[action[0]] + '.' + case['getter'] + '()'
        if case['prepare']:
            act = 'r.Apply(' + act + ',r.Value{})'
        main = f'''package main
import(r "gopurs/output/gopurs_runtime"; {imports})
func main(){{
 act:={act}
 for i:=0;i<3;i++{{if value:=r.Apply(act,r.Value{{}});value.Type!=r.TypeInt||value.IntVal!={case['expected']}{{panic("invalid global warmup result")}}}}
 describe:=r.Apply({aliases[console[0]]}.Get_Effect_Console_log(),r.Str("{case['label']}"))
 r.Apply({aliases[bench[0]]}.Call_Bench_runBench(describe,act),r.Value{{}})
}}
'''
        source = PROOF / (key + '-' + side + '-main.go')
        source.write_text(main)
        sources[key][side] = sha(source)
        command = ['go', 'build', '-pgo=off', '-o', str(PROOF / (key + '-' + side + '-probe')), str(source)]
        process = subprocess.run(command, cwd=builds[case['source_suite']][side] / 'output', env=env, text=True, capture_output=True)
        (PROOF / (key + '-' + side + '-build.stdout')).write_text(process.stdout)
        (PROOF / (key + '-' + side + '-build.stderr')).write_text(process.stderr)
        process.check_returncode()
        assert not process.stderr
        commands[key][side] = command
        print('Built', key, side, flush=True)

# All probe builds complete before the first timed process.
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / 'bin/benchmark'))
from validate import ROW
order = ['before', 'after', 'after', 'before', 'before', 'after']
results = {}
for case in cases:
    key = case['key']
    samples, runs = {'before': [], 'after': []}, []
    for index, side in enumerate(order, 1):
        process = subprocess.run([str(PROOF / (key + '-' + side + '-probe'))],
                                 cwd=builds[case['source_suite']][side] / 'output', env=env,
                                 text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=60)
        stem = f'{key}-{index}-{side}'
        (PROOF / (stem + '.stdout')).write_text(process.stdout)
        (PROOF / (stem + '.stderr')).write_text(process.stderr)
        process.check_returncode()
        assert not process.stderr
        values = ROW.findall(process.stdout)
        assert len(values) == 1 and process.stdout.count('(Test)') == 1
        label, value, elapsed = values[0]
        assert label.strip() == case['label'] and value.strip() == str(case['expected'])
        elapsed = float(elapsed)
        assert math.isfinite(elapsed) and elapsed > 0
        batches = [int(n) for n in re.findall(r'^Batch iterations: (\d+)$', process.stdout, re.M)]
        assert len(batches) == 1 and 0 < batches[0] <= 16777216 and not batches[0] & (batches[0] - 1)
        samples[side].append(elapsed)
        runs.append({'variant': side, 'time_us': elapsed, 'batch_iterations': batches[0],
                     'stdout': process.stdout, 'stderr': process.stderr})
        print(stem, elapsed, 'us', flush=True)
    medians = {side: statistics.median(values) for side, values in samples.items()}
    change = 100 * (medians['after'] / medians['before'] - 1)
    results[key] = {'case': case['label'], 'source_suite': case['source_suite'], 'expected': case['expected'],
                    'original_builds': originals[case['source_suite']], 'commands': commands[key],
                    'main_sha256': sources[key], 'probe_binary_sha256': {side: sha(PROOF / (key + '-' + side + '-probe')) for side in samples},
                    'order': order, 'samples_us': samples, 'medians_us': medians, 'change_percent': change,
                    'primary_change_percent': case['primary_change_percent'], 'increase_over_5_percent_reproduced': change > 5,
                    'runs': runs}
for scope, pair in builds.items():
    for side, path in pair.items():
        assert originals[scope][side] == HELPERS['inventory'](path)['provenance']
assert sha(primary) == primary_sha
result = {'measured_at_utc': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
          'scope': 'Separate diagnostics only; original primary samples and aggregates remain unchanged',
          'protocol': 'AB/BA/AB for each case; actual getters and unchanged timed measureBatch; runBench is byte-identical or has only separately verified call lowering outside the timer; 3 global warmups then calibration and minimum of ten batches; all builds finished before timing',
          'GOGC': '800', 'GOMAXPROCS': 'default', 'host_isolated': False,
          'source_comparison': 'generated-comparison.json', 'script_sha256': sha(__file__),
          'primary_campaign_sha256': primary_sha, 'cases': results, 'oracles_verified': 6 * len(cases),
          'original_generated_sources_and_binaries_unchanged': True}
(PROOF / 'results.json').write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + '\n')
print(json.dumps({key: {name: row[name] for name in ['case', 'source_suite', 'samples_us', 'medians_us', 'change_percent', 'increase_over_5_percent_reproduced']}
                  for key, row in results.items()}, indent=2))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pair frozen Go App/AppAll builds against all 37 unchanged archived C medians."""
import argparse
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
from pathlib import Path
import platform
import runpy
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
ROOT = Path('/Users/0x1/Documents/htdocs/altbak.pub')
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / 'bin/benchmark'))
C = runpy.run_path(str(ROOT / 'bin/benchmark/compare-core.py'))
J = runpy.run_path(str(ROOT / 'bin/benchmark/js-ratios.py'))


def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def write(path, value):
    Path(path).write_text(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + '\n')


def metrics(times, reference):
    if set(times) != set(reference) or len(times) not in (14, 37):
        raise ValueError('Identical Go/C case populations of 14 or 37 required')
    ratios = [times[name] / reference[name] for name in times]
    if any(not math.isfinite(x) or x <= 0 for x in ratios):
        raise ValueError('Invalid ratio')
    return {'total': sum(times.values()) / sum(reference.values()),
            'arithmetic': statistics.mean(ratios), 'median': statistics.median(ratios),
            'geometric': math.exp(statistics.mean(math.log(x) for x in ratios))}


def verify_freeze(frozen):
    if 'benchmark_baseline_manifest' in frozen:
        benchmark_manifest=Path(frozen['benchmark_baseline_manifest'])
        assert sha(benchmark_manifest)==frozen['benchmark_baseline_manifest_sha256']
        baseline_benchmark=json.loads(benchmark_manifest.read_text())
        for name,entry in baseline_benchmark['preserved_existing_files'].items():
            assert sha(entry['snapshot'])==entry['sha256'], ('Changed benchmark snapshot',name)
            if name!='README.md':
                assert sha(ROOT/name)==entry['sha256'], ('Changed prior publication',name)
    baseline_path = Path(frozen['compiler_baseline_manifest'])
    if sha(baseline_path) != frozen['compiler_baseline_manifest_sha256']:
        raise ValueError('Compiler baseline manifest changed')
    baseline = json.loads(baseline_path.read_text())
    for group in ['files', 'sources']:
        C['verify_hashes']({entry['path']: entry['sha256'] for entry in baseline[group].values()})
    C['verify_hashes'](frozen['source_sha256'], ROOT)
    C['verify_hashes'](frozen['library_sources_sha256'])
    C['verify_hashes'](frozen['reference_files_sha256'])
    for build in [frozen['go_before_core'], frozen['c_build']]:
        C['verify_hashes']({build['manifest_path']: build['manifest_sha256']})
        C['verify_hashes'](build['payload_sha256'])
    old_all = frozen['go_before_all']
    path = Path(old_all['directory'])
    C['verify_hashes']({str(path / 'manifest.json'): old_all['manifest_sha256'],
                       str(path / 'benchmark'): old_all['manifest']['binary_sha256']})


def compiler_snapshot():
    root = ROOT.parent / 'gopurs/gopurs'
    paths = [root / 'bin/gopurs-native', root / 'bin/gopurs.js', root / 'bin/gopurs']
    paths += [path for folder in ['src', 'runtime'] for path in sorted((root / folder).rglob('*'))
              if path.is_file() and path.suffix in {'.purs', '.go', '.js', '.rs'}]
    return {'root': str(root),
            'head': subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(root), 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], text=True).strip(),
            'files_sha256': {str(path): sha(path) for path in paths}}


def plan_entry(key, build):
    return {'key': key, 'mode': 'pure', 'command': build['command'],
            'artifact': build['cwd'], 'cwd': build['cwd'],
            'manifest': build['manifest_path'], 'manifest_sha256': build['manifest_sha256'],
            'payload_sha256': build['payload_sha256'],
            'executable_sha256': build['manifest']['binary_sha256']}


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--freeze', type=Path, default=Path(__file__).with_name('freeze.json'))
    parser.add_argument('--after-core', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--after-all', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--execute', action='store_true', help='run only after all builds and tests have finished')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    frozen = json.loads(args.freeze.read_text())
    verify_freeze(frozen)
    before_core = C['inspect_go'](Path(frozen['go_before_core']['cwd']))
    after_core = C['inspect_go'](args.after_core.resolve())
    before_all = J['inspect'](Path(frozen['go_before_all']['directory']))
    after_all = J['inspect'](args.after_all.resolve())
    for label, before, after in [('core', before_core['manifest'], after_core['manifest']),
                                 ('all', before_all, after_all)]:
        for field in ['profile', 'toolchain']:
            if before[field] != after[field]:
                raise ValueError(f'{label} build {field} differs')
        for name in before['inputs']:
            if name.startswith(('src/', 'srx/')) and before['inputs'][name] != after['inputs'].get(name):
                raise ValueError(f'{label} benchmark input differs: {name}')
    if before_core['command'] == after_core['command'] or Path(frozen['go_before_all']['directory']) == args.after_all.resolve():
        raise ValueError('Distinct before/after builds are required')
    plan = [plan_entry('before', before_core), plan_entry('after', after_core)]
    if not args.execute:
        print(json.dumps({'validated': True, 'core_plan': plan,
                          'all_pair': [frozen['go_before_all']['directory'], str(args.after_all.resolve())],
                          'C_reference_remeasured': False, 'processes': 12}, indent=2))
        return
    args.output = args.output.resolve()
    args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    write(args.output / 'freeze.json', frozen)
    write(args.output / 'core-plan.json', plan)
    env = dict(os.environ, GOGC='800')
    for key in ['GOMAXPROCS', 'PPROF']:
        env.pop(key, None)
    compiler = compiler_snapshot()
    started = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    load_start = list(os.getloadavg())
    commands = [
        [sys.executable, '-B', str(ROOT / 'bin/benchmark/measure.py'), '--plan',
         str(args.output / 'core-plan.json'), '--output', str(args.output / 'core')],
        [sys.executable, '-B', str(Path(__file__).with_name('collect-all.py')), '--before',
         frozen['go_before_all']['directory'], '--after', str(args.after_all.resolve()),
         '--output', str(args.output / 'all')],
    ]
    for command in commands:
        verify_freeze(frozen)
        C['verify_hashes'](compiler['files_sha256'])
        subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, env=env, check=True)
        verify_freeze(frozen)
        C['verify_hashes'](compiler['files_sha256'])
    core = json.loads((args.output / 'core/results.json').read_text())
    all_cases = json.loads((args.output / 'all/results.json').read_text())
    labels = C['ROWS']
    core_times = {variant: dict(zip(labels, data['times_us'])) for variant, data in core.items()}
    core_aggregates = {variant: metrics(times, frozen['c_times_us']) for variant, times in core_times.items()}
    core_historical = metrics(frozen['historical_go_core_times_us'], frozen['c_times_us'])
    for key, value in core_historical.items():
        if not math.isclose(value, frozen['historical_aggregates'][key], rel_tol=1e-12):
            raise ValueError('Historical metrics do not reproduce the official archive')
    # Preserve the publication's primary App medians for core14, and use AppAll
    # for library23 only. Both sides of every aggregate now contain all 37 cases.
    matched37 = {
        variant: {name: core_times[variant][name] if name in core_times[variant]
                  else row['medians_us'][variant]
                  for name, row in all_cases['all_tests'].items()}
        for variant in ('before', 'after')}
    aggregates = {variant: metrics(times, frozen['c37_times_us']) for variant, times in matched37.items()}
    historical = metrics(frozen['historical_go37_times_us'], frozen['c37_times_us'])
    for key, prior_key in [('total', '/'), ('arithmetic', 'μ'), ('median', 'Q₂'), ('geometric', 'G')]:
        if not math.isclose(historical[key], frozen['historical37_aggregates'][prior_key], rel_tol=1e-12):
            raise ValueError('Historical 37-case metrics do not reproduce the official README')
    rows = []
    for name in matched37['after']:
        before, after = matched37['before'][name], matched37['after'][name]
        if name in labels:
            index = labels.index(name)
            samples = {variant: [sample['times_us'][index] for sample in core[variant]['process_runs']]
                       for variant in ['before', 'after']}
        else:
            samples = all_cases['all_tests'][name]['samples_us']
        rows.append({'case': name, 'times_us': {'before': before, 'after': after, 'c': frozen['c37_times_us'][name]},
                     'go_over_c': {variant: times[name] / frozen['c37_times_us'][name] for variant, times in matched37.items()},
                     'samples_us': samples, 'speedup': before / after, 'change_percent': 100 * (after / before - 1),
                     'before_over_historical': before / frozen['historical_go37_times_us'][name]})
    all_regressions = sorted([{'case': name, 'change_percent': case['change_percent'],
                              'medians_us': case['medians_us'], 'samples_us': case['samples_us']}
                             for name, case in all_cases['all_tests'].items() if case['change_percent'] > 5],
                            key=lambda row: -row['change_percent'])
    raw_core = {path.name: path.read_text() for suffix in ['stdout', 'stderr']
                for path in sorted((args.output / 'core').glob('*.' + suffix))}
    report = {'started_at_utc': started, 'completed_at_utc': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
              'host': platform.platform(), 'machine': platform.machine(), 'host_isolated': False,
              'load_average_start': load_start, 'load_average_end': list(os.getloadavg()),
              'protocol': {'paired_order': 'AB/BA/AB', 'processes_per_build': 3,
                           'primary': '14 App core medians plus 23 AppAll library medians; all four Go/C aggregates use 37 matched cases',
                           'GOGC': '800', 'GOMAXPROCS': 'default', 'pgo': False,
                           'C_reference_remeasured': False, 'JS_reference_remeasured': False,
                           'aggregation': 'median of three process minima for each case'},
              'commands': commands, 'wrapper_sha256': sha(Path(__file__)),
              'frozen_reference': frozen, 'compiler_snapshot': compiler, 'aggregates': aggregates, 'historical_aggregates': historical,
              'primary_times_us': core_times, 'primary_total_ms': {k: sum(v.values())/1000 for k,v in core_times.items()},
              'matched37_times_us': matched37, 'matched37_total_ms': {k: sum(v.values())/1000 for k,v in matched37.items()},
              'core14_aggregates': core_aggregates, 'historical_core14_aggregates': core_historical,
              'c_total_ms': sum(frozen['c37_times_us'].values())/1000,
              'rows_by_go_c_descending': sorted(rows, key=lambda r: -r['go_over_c']['after']),
              'all_case_regressions_over_5_percent': all_regressions,
              'validation': {'processes': 12, 'core_oracles': 84, 'all_oracles': 222,
                             'total_oracles': 306, 'source_and_binary_guards': True},
              'core_manifest': json.loads((args.output / 'core/manifest.json').read_text()),
              'core_campaign': core, 'raw_core_outputs': raw_core, 'all_campaign': all_cases}
    write(args.output / 'results.json', report)
    print(json.dumps({'aggregates': aggregates, 'historical': historical,
                      'totals_ms': report['matched37_total_ms'], 'c_total_ms': report['c_total_ms'],
                      'all_regressions_over_5_percent': all_regressions}, indent=2))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

action='store_true', help='publish after all validation; default only archives the proposal') args = parser.parse_args() campaign_bytes = args.campaign.read_bytes() campaign = json.loads(campaign_bytes) reference_path = Path(__file__).with_name('references.json') reference_bytes = reference_path.read_bytes() frozen = campaign['frozen_reference'] require(sha(reference_bytes) == frozen['reference_files_sha256'][str(reference_path)], 'The frozen JavaScript reference file changed') publisher = ROOT / 'bin/benchmark/publish.py' require(sha(publisher.read_bytes()) == capture; review the new edits') else: pre_publication.write_bytes(original) audit = {'created_at_utc': now.isoformat(), 'mode': 'write' if args.write else 'dry-run', 'readme': sha(publisher.read_bytes()), 'references_sha256': sha(reference_bytes), 'readme_before_sha256': sha(original), 'readme_proposed_sha256': sha(proposed), 'initial_snapshot_sha256': sha(snapshot.read_bytes()) if snapshot.exists() else None, 'input_policy': 'Read the live README; never restore the initial snapshot; preserve all non-target bytes.', 'external_edits': external, False} (output / 'README.frozen.md').write_bytes(snapshot.read_bytes()) (output / 'README.input.md').write_bytes(original) (output / 'external-readme-edits.patch').write_text(external_diff) (output / indent=2)) if __name__ == '__main__': try: main() except (ValueError, KeyError, OSError) as error: print('ERROR: ' + str(error), file=sys.stderr) sys.exit(1)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read-only independent consistency checks for the archived hot-path campaign."""
import base64, hashlib, json, runpy, sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
WORK = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
ROOT = WORK.parents[2]
path = ROOT / 'docs/benchmark-results/2026-11-27-go-record-consumer.json'
raw = path.read_bytes()
archive = json.loads(raw)
sha = lambda data: hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
count = 0


def visit(value):
    global count
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        if isinstance(value.get('text'), str) and 'sha256' in value:
            assert sha(value['text'].encode()) == value['sha256']
            count += 1
        if isinstance(value.get('base64'), str) and 'sha256' in value:
            assert sha(base64.b64decode(value['base64'])) == value['sha256']
        for child in value.values():
            visit(child)
    elif isinstance(value, list):
        for child in value:
            visit(child)


visit(archive)
helper = runpy.run_path(str(Path(__file__).with_name('archive.py')))
checks = helper['check_campaign'](archive['campaign'])
assert checks == archive['validation']['archive_checks']
for name,check in [('runtime_input_proofs',lambda:helper['check_inputs'](archive['campaign'])),('alias_input_proofs',lambda:helper['check_alias_inputs'](archive['campaign'])),('compact_alias_input_proofs',lambda:helper['check_alias_inputs'](archive['campaign'],compact=True))]:
    if archive['validation'][name].get('performed') is not False:
        assert check()==archive['validation'][name]
    else:
        assert archive['validation'][name]['total_oracles']==0
for key, alias in [('array_input_proofs',False),('array_alias_input_proofs',True)]:
    if archive['validation'][key].get('performed') is not False:
        assert helper['check_array_inputs'](archive['campaign'],alias=alias)==archive['validation'][key]
    else:assert archive['validation'][key]['total_oracles']==0
for key,fn in [('sum_input_proofs',lambda:helper['check_sum_inputs'](archive['campaign'])),('sum_wide_input_proofs',lambda:helper['check_sum_inputs'](archive['campaign'],wide=True)),('tree_input_proofs',lambda:helper['check_tree_inputs'](archive['campaign']))]:
    if archive['validation'][key].get('performed') is not False:assert fn()==archive['validation'][key]
    else:assert archive['validation'][key]['total_oracles']==0
for key,wide in [('traverse_input_proofs',False),('traverse_wide_input_proofs',True)]:
    if archive['validation'][key].get('performed') is not False:assert helper['check_traverse_inputs'](archive['campaign'],wide=wide)==archive['validation'][key]
    else:assert archive['validation'][key]['total_oracles']==0
for key,fn in [('codepoint_take_input_proofs','check_codepoint_take_inputs'),('loop_input_proofs','check_loop_inputs'),('ref_input_proofs','check_ref_inputs')]:
    if archive['validation'][key].get('performed') is not False:assert helper[fn](archive['campaign'])==archive['validation'][key]
for case in ['map','traverse']:
    for wide in [False,True]:
        entry=archive['validation']['lanes_input_proofs'][case+('-wide' if wide else '')]
        if entry.get('performed') is not False:assert helper['check_lanes_inputs'](archive['campaign'],case,wide)==entry
if archive['validation']['concat_input_proofs'].get('performed') is not False:assert helper['check_concat_inputs'](archive['campaign'])==archive['validation']['concat_input_proofs']
assert helper['check_record_consumer_inputs'](archive['campaign'])==archive['validation']['record_consumer_input_proofs']
assert helper['check_excluded_campaign'](archive['campaign'])==archive['validation']['excluded_campaigns']
assert helper['check_diagnostics'](archive['campaign']) == archive['validation']['diagnostic_checks']

# Independent record-consumer validation

Four generator unit tests pass, including 11,340 paired Go observations. The module uses unrelated names and complete integer rows with one, two and eight fields. Cases include zero/positive/negative constant deltas, multiple updated fields, record-first parameter order, boxed and native counters, and Int32Max times Int32Max (above exact floating-point precision). Reference consumers preserve the original worker plus the complete projections, with a pure identity call preventing the new fusion.

The runtime matrix covers seven full-width seeds, nine terminating counts, ten record shapes and two action replays for nine consumers. It checks compact and general layouts, reversed/duplicate/missing keys, short/nil value payloads, maps and JSONObject getters. Getter order, mutable getters, thrown sentinel identity, panic observations and input effect replay agree with the unfused reference. The count -1 and nonzero counts with low32==0 are deliberately not executed: the unchanged cold worker stops at zero and these would require approximately2^32iterations.

Admission tests reject missing/duplicated projections, additional constants/uses, unknown calls, intermediate Lets, saved-effect construction, foreign workers, staged arguments and recursive contexts. Explicit contradictory Update and Effect annotations are rejected. The real residual `Effect a` annotation beneath `Effect Int` is admitted. A direct emitter test asserts that EffectPure outside an executing effect block is rejected before translating anything or consuming identifiers.

The source fixture has 44 observations, independently calculated by an imperative integer oracle and compared with source JavaScript. It exercises opaque Ref inputs, immutable originals, multiple consumers, saved actions replayed after Ref.write, extra uses, unknown calls and an intervening effect. Initial Release and Dev compilation pass. A Release-only intramodule recurrence change from delta1 to delta2 matches source JavaScript and a clean rebuild after a warm build. Final native repetition passes 2/2 in56.36seconds using the combined compiler. Both initial profiles and the Release warm/clean transition agree with the same44-observation source oracle. All six sources/tests, compiler binaries and runtime remain unchanged across the run. `e2e-native/result.json` records hashes, commands, timing and the12retained phases.

Diagnostic history is retained. The first generated test detected no activation because the fallback returned a boxed Int; the actual source test then detected a residual generic Effect annotation not handled by the initial guard. Both were corrected before the final assertions passed. Small fixture-only errors during test construction (RecordDict2 argument order and a NeutralExpr newtype conversion) were corrected without changing production semantics. No benchmark, C or FFI sources were edited by these tests.

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). # 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Observe an intentional external alias mutation inside the real opaque count effect."""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys

def digest(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()

def main():
    parser=argparse.ArgumentParser();parser.add_argument('build',type=Path);parser.add_argument('proof',type=Path);args=parser.parse_args()
    proof=args.proof.resolve()
    generator=Path(__file__).with_name('record-input-proof.py')
    subprocess.run([sys.executable,str(generator),str(args.build),str(proof),'--prepare-only'],check=True,capture_output=True,text=True)
    manifest=json.loads((proof/'manifest.json').read_text())
    widths={'RecordSetSmall1000':2,'RecordSetMedium1000':8,'RecordSetLarge1000':16}
    inputs=[]
    for name,width in widths.items():
        fields=[list(range(1,width+1)),[2147483647 if i%2==0 else -2147483648 for i in range(width)]]
        for count in [0,1,7]:
            for values in fields:
                for layout in ['dictionary','map']:
                    inputs.append({'case':len(inputs),'name':name,'count':count,'fields':values,'layout':layout})
    (proof/'inputs.json').write_text(json.dumps(inputs,indent=2)+'\n')
    override=proof/'opaque-override.go';text=override.read_text()
    assert text.count('RecordAuditCalls++')==1
    text=text.replace('RecordAuditCalls++','RecordAuditCalls++\n        if RecordAuditCalls == 2 && RecordAuditMutation != nil { RecordAuditMutation() }')
    text+='\nvar RecordAuditMutation func()\n';override.write_text(text)
    original=next(iter(json.loads((proof/'overlay.json').read_text())['Replace']))
    import difflib
    (proof/'opaque-override.patch').write_text(''.join(difflib.unified_diff(Path(original).read_text().splitlines(True),text.splitlines(True),fromfile=original,tofile=str(override))))
    program=(proof/'main.go').read_text()
    old='action:=actions[input.Name];original:=record(input,prepared[input.Name]);unchanged(original,input)\n   for _,path:=range []string{"Apply","ffi_conversion","forced_fallback"}{'
    assert program.count(old)==1
    boundary=program.split('.RecordAuditInputs=',1)[0].split()[-1]
    replacement='''action:=actions[input.Name]
   for _,path:=range []string{"Apply","ffi_conversion","forced_fallback"}{
     original:=record(input,prepared[input.Name]);unchanged(original,input)
     alias:=original;mutations:=0
     BOUNDARY.RecordAuditMutation=func(){mutations++;mutateRecord(alias,string(rune('a'+len(input.Fields)-1)))}'''.replace('BOUNDARY',boundary)
    program=program.replace(old,replacement)
    oldcheck='unchanged(original,input)\n     fmt.Printf'
    assert program.count(oldcheck)==1
    program=program.replace(oldcheck,'''if mutations!=1{panic("alias mutation effect count")}
     changed:=input;changed.Fields=append([]int64{},input.Fields...);last:=len(changed.Fields)-1;changed.Fields[last]=int64(int32(changed.Fields[last]+17))
     unchanged(original,changed);unchanged(alias,changed)
     fmt.Printf''')
    program+='''
func mutateRecord(value r.Value,key string){
 switch value.Type {
 case r.TypeRecordData:
  data:=(*r.RecordData)(value.UnsafePtr);for i,label:=range data.Keys{if label==key{data.Vals[i]=r.Int(int64(int32(data.Vals[i].IntVal+17)));return}}
 case r.TypeRecord:
  data:=*(*map[string]r.Value)(value.UnsafePtr);data[key]=r.Int(int64(int32(data[key].IntVal+17)));return
 }
 panic("unexpected alias mutation representation")
}
'''

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Exercise both compact two-field payloads at the real opaque count boundary."""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys

def digest(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()

def main():
    parser=argparse.ArgumentParser();parser.add_argument('build',type=Path);parser.add_argument('proof',type=Path);args=parser.parse_args()
    proof=args.proof.resolve()
    generator=Path(__file__).with_name('record-input-proof.py')
    subprocess.run([sys.executable,str(generator),str(args.build),str(proof),'--prepare-only'],check=True,capture_output=True,text=True)
    manifest=json.loads((proof/'manifest.json').read_text())
    widths={'RecordSetSmall1000':2}
    inputs=[]
    for name,width in widths.items():
        fields=[list(range(1,width+1)),[2147483647 if i%2==0 else -2147483648 for i in range(width)]]
        for count in [0,1,7]:
            for values in fields:
                for layout in ['shape','boxed2']:
                    inputs.append({'case':len(inputs),'name':name,'count':count,'fields':values,'layout':layout})
    (proof/'inputs.json').write_text(json.dumps(inputs,indent=2)+'\n')
    override=proof/'opaque-override.go';text=override.read_text()
    assert text.count('RecordAuditCalls++')==1
    text=text.replace('RecordAuditCalls++','RecordAuditCalls++\n        if RecordAuditCalls == 2 && RecordAuditMutation != nil { RecordAuditMutation() }')
    text+='\nvar RecordAuditMutation func()\n';override.write_text(text)
    original=next(iter(json.loads((proof/'overlay.json').read_text())['Replace']))
    import difflib
    (proof/'opaque-override.patch').write_text(''.join(difflib.unified_diff(Path(original).read_text().splitlines(True),text.splitlines(True),fromfile=original,tofile=str(override))))
    program=(proof/'main.go').read_text()
    program=program.replace('import("encoding/json";', 'import("encoding/json";"unsafe";')
    marker='if input.Layout=="map"{return r.Record(fields)}'
    assert program.count(marker)==1
    program=program.replace(marker,marker+'''\n if input.Layout=="boxed2"{return r.Value{Type:r.TypeRecord2,UnsafePtr:unsafe.Pointer(&r.RecordData2{RecordKeys2:&r.RecordKeys2{K0:keys[0],K1:keys[1]},V0:values[0],V1:values[1]})}}''')
    old='action:=actions[input.Name];original:=record(input,prepared[input.Name]);unchanged(original,input)\n   for _,path:=range []string{"Apply","ffi_conversion","forced_fallback"}{'
    assert program.count(old)==1
    boundary=program.split('.RecordAuditInputs=',1)[0].split()[-1]
    replacement='''action:=actions[input.Name]
   for _,path:=range []string{"Apply","ffi_conversion","forced_fallback"}{
     original:=record(input,prepared[input.Name]);unchanged(original,input)
     alias:=original;mutations:=0
     BOUNDARY.RecordAuditMutation=func(){mutations++;mutateRecord(alias,string(rune('a'+len(input.Fields)-1)))}'''.replace('BOUNDARY',boundary)
    program=program.replace(old,replacement)
    oldcheck='unchanged(original,input)\n     fmt.Printf'
    assert program.count(oldcheck)==1
    program=program.replace(oldcheck,'''if mutations!=1{panic("alias mutation effect count")}
     changed:=input;changed.Fields=append([]int64{},input.Fields...);last:=len(changed.Fields)-1;changed.Fields[last]=int64(int32(changed.Fields[last]+17))
     unchanged(original,changed);unchanged(alias,changed)
     fmt.Printf''')
    program+='''
func mutateRecord(value r.Value,key string){
 switch value.Type {
 case r.TypeRecord2:
  if value.IntVal==1{data:=(*r.RecordData2Int)(value.UnsafePtr);if key==data.K0{data.V0=int64(int32(data.V0+17));return};if key==data.K1{data.V1=int64(int32(data.V1+17));return}}else{data:=(*r.RecordData2)(value.UnsafePtr);if key==data.K0{data.V0=r.Int(int64(int32(data.V0.IntVal+17)));return};if key==data.K1{data.V1=r.Int(int64(int32(data.V1.IntVal+17)));return}}
 case r.TypeRecordData:
  data:=(*r.RecordData)(value.UnsafePtr);for i,label:=range data.Keys{if label==key{data.Vals[i]=r.Int(int64(int32(data.Vals[i].IntVal+17)));return}}
 case r.TypeRecord:
  data:=*(*map[string]r.Value)(value.UnsafePtr);data[key]=r.Int(int64(int32(data[key].IntVal+17)));return
 }
 panic("unexpected alias mutation representation")
}
'''
    (proof/'main.go').write_text(program)
    oracle=(proof/'oracle.mjs').read_text();assert oracle.count('let original=0;')==1
    oracle=oracle.replace('let original=0;','fields[fields.length-1]=(fields[fields.length-1]+17)|0;\n  let original=0;')
    (proof/'oracle.mjs').write_text(oracle)
    assert all(digest(k)==v for k,v in manifest['generated_source_sha256'].items())
    result=subprocess.run(manifest['command'],cwd=Path(manifest['build'])/'output',env={**os.environ,'GOWORK':'off'},text=True,capture_output=True,timeout=120)
    (proof/'stdout.txt').write_text(result.stdout);(proof/'stderr.txt').write_text(result.stderr);assert result.returncode==0,result.stderr
    expected=subprocess.check_output(['node',str(proof/'oracle.mjs'),str(proof/'inputs.json')],text=True);(proof/'expected.txt').write_text(expected);assert result.stdout==expected
    assert all(digest(k)==v for k,v in manifest['generated_source_sha256'].items());assert digest(Path(manifest['build'])/'benchmark')==manifest['binary_sha256']
    manifest.update(validated=True,input_variants=len(inputs),oracles=len(inputs)*3,record_representations=['shape-int2','legacy-boxed2'],counter_domain=[0,1,7],inputs_immutable=False,external_alias_mutation_observed_once=True,compiler_added_mutation=False,override_sha256=digest(override),mutation_delta=17)
    manifest['action_opaque_calls_per_case']={'RecordSetSmall1000':2}
    manifest['action_cases']=['RecordSetSmall1000']
    manifest['limitation']='A diagnostic overlay mutates the input through an alias inside opaqueValue when the count effect actually runs. Both the original boxed path and the new direct worker invoke that same effect body. The caller must observe this intentional external mutation once, before record projection and consumption; no mutation is added by the compiler. Benchmark/FFI sources and official generated builds remain unchanged.'
    manifest['artifact_sha256']={p.name:digest(p) for p in proof.iterdir() if p.is_file() and p.name!='manifest.json'}
    (proof/'manifest.json').write_text(json.dumps(manifest,indent=2)+'\n')
    print(f'{len(inputs)*3} compact alias-boundary controls passed; both RecordInt2 and legacy boxed payloads observe the count mutation once.')

if __name__=='__main__':main()

campaign/core/README.before.md.text:
# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript
